Exercise C.3 — A Gaussian posterior and a safety probability
      
      
        Prior $f\sim\mathcal N(0,1)$. Four measurements $y_i=f+\varepsilon_i$ with $\varepsilon_i\sim\mathcal N(0,0.25)$ i.i.d. and independent of $f$ have mean $\bar y=0.9$. (a) Compute the posterior mean and variance with precision addition. (b) Compute $\mathbb P(f\lt0.5\mid\text{data})$. (c) Is $f\ge0.3$ certified by the lower bound $\mu-2\sigma$, and what is the posterior probability that this bound fails?
        
          Show answer
          
            (a) $\bar y$ has noise variance $0.25/4=0.0625$, i.e. precision $16$. Posterior precision $1+16=17$, variance $1/17=0.0588$ (standard deviation $0.2425$), mean $(1\cdot0+16\cdot0.9)/17=0.847$.
            (b) $\Phi\big((0.5-0.847)/0.2425\big)=\Phi(-1.431)=0.076$.
            (c) $\mu-2\sigma=0.847-0.485=0.362\ge0.3$, so yes. The bound fails with posterior probability $\Phi(-2)=0.023$. This is a Bayesian statement inside the model; a whole run of such decisions needs a union bound over them (Section 6).

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Actual arbitrary-space independent latent and four iid Gaussian noises generate the true full reading tuple law and its posterior disintegration.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The proof derives the actual four-noise product law from mutual independence, pushes the independent prior/noise pair through literal reading addition, and composes the genuine swapped-joint disintegration. It does not assume the desired posterior law.
hypotheses: The source model has prior N(0,1), four mutually independent noise variables each N(0,1/4), and independence of the latent variable from the noise family. The arbitrary-space bridge uses exactly HasLaw, iIndepFun and IndepFun of latent with the actual noise tuple.

Conditioning is represented by the explicitly derived everywhere-defined Gaussian posterior kernel, obtained from the genuine full joint disintegration and normalized likelihood. No uniqueness of arbitrary conditional versions at an individual null data observation is asserted.
The four given readings need only have average9/10. Their individual values are not otherwise restricted; the likelihood and derived kernel depend on their actual sum.

The exact posterior is N(72/85,1/17), sigma=sqrt(1/17)>0, and lower=72/85-2sqrt(1/17). Decimal parameters, standardized arguments and probabilities are approximations; the original unqualified equalities are retained as explicit whole-source gaps.

The single-decision probability is posterior probability within the stated model. The joint-run warning is a generic union aggregation instruction, not a constructed adaptive posterior law or frequentist confidence guarantee.
